10.t: Working with data: mitochondria in different cells
q: Calculate how many times more of the cell volume is mitochondria in heart muscle than in liver.
Explain why heart muscle cells have many mitochondria with large cristae.
The heart contracts non-stop, so it needs a constant supply of ATP from aerobic respiration; cristae give a large surface for the electron transport chain and ATP synthase.
Suggest why the athlete’s skeletal muscle has more mitochondria.
Endurance training increases the demand for ATP, and muscle responds by making more mitochondria.
Explain how red blood cells make ATP without mitochondria, and suggest one advantage.
By anaerobic respiration (glycolysis) in the cytoplasm. Advantage: they do not use the oxygen they carry, and there is more room for haemoglobin.
Predict the amount of mitochondria in the midpiece and head of a sperm cell. Explain.
Many in the midpiece, none in the head: the midpiece supplies ATP to the flagellum for swimming; the head carries the nucleus and acrosome.
